added_claims.claim: Before acting, Elliott studies the local culture of capitalism and corporate control in each country, plus how the board and management got there and why they are failing, because receptiveness to shareholder-driven change varies by market.

added_claims.claim: Engagement tactics vary: some campaigns stay under the radar and are disclosed only to the company, others involve public position filings, depending on the rules and strategy, and usually start with a detailed discussion and a long presentation deck.

added_claims.quote: when we win um the shareholders win the the days of green mail are uh longer
added_claims.claim: Modern activism differs from greenmail: when the activist wins, all shareholders gain, and accountability campaigns are rare because few investors still act as owners.

added_claims.quote: the dealer had several other people um in the trade
added_claims.claim: The Japanese linker arbitrage was shown by a dealer who already had several other investors in it, so it was a crowded trade that looked obviously cheap on the trading floor before it fell 30%, forcing others out.

added_claims.speaker: Paul Singer
added_claims.quote: I I had a lot of pressure to onewind the trade but I kept the trade
added_claims.claim: Daily mark-to-market makes holding a losing convergent trade a matter of skill: pressure to unwind was heavy and many were sold out, but Singer kept the position through the 2008 do-or-die period and notes it requires a different skill set from managers.

added_claims.speaker: Paul Singer
added_claims.quote: you can't get bored by not losing serious money
added_claims.claim: Avoiding large losses also preserves the manager's emotional energy: burnout comes largely from being drained by adversity, so a capital-preservation culture lengthens a career and sustains judgment.

added_claims.claim: In the Argentine restructuring about 60,000 bondholders took part at the end of the two offers, including five hedge funds of which Elliott was the largest, and Elliott's cost basis was already in the teens to 30s as bonds kept falling.

added_claims.claim: Central bank money, though created from nothing, has sovereign backing because taxes and the army are paid in it, so government embrace of cryptocurrencies means endorsing alternatives to sovereign money and risks undermining the dollar's reserve role; Singer finds it paradoxical that the US itself supports an alternative.

corrections.issue: Reframed: Singer did not say Argentina had defaulted only 3 or 4 times; he said Elliott knew it had a history of default (three or four times in 150 years) but judged default unlikely given its resources, as it was then the 7th or 8th largest economy, and the market view was default.
corrections.fix: Elliott bought performing Argentine bonds trading in the 70s to 80s, aware of a history of default 3 to 4 times in 150 years, but judged default unlikely because of the country's size and resources; the country defaulted and the bonds collapsed.

corrections.issue: Unsupported inference: Singer only says that about 25% of holders held out, that the country told them they would get nothing if they did not accept, and that a second offer three years later on the same terms gave a few percent more; he does not say here that holding out eventually recovered more.
corrections.fix: About 25% of Argentine holders held out; the country said it was this offer or nothing and repeated essentially the same offer about three years later (a few percent more), after which holdouts litigated for years.
